top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a clean mechanism (magic-wavelength trapping lets many neutral atoms be confined in the Lamb-Dicke regime with vanishing first-order differential light shift), driven to about 1e-18 uncertainty and reproduced across independent laboratories, with a compact two-name allocation (Katori, Ye) and a citation that separates it from the 2005 and 2012 clock-related prizes. IceCube (P002) is a real discovery but the source origin of the diffuse flux is still largely open and confirmation is within one detector; I rank it above no award because it is solid science that could mature, and a prize this year is preferable to none.
